atoms.reference: The only rule is to share at least one novel and the source code; the code need not be licensed in a particular way; the 'novel' is defined however the participant wants, a random Project Gutenberg novel included; copyright to be respected and not policed.

evidence.record_quote: The only rule is that you share at least one novel and also your source code at the end.
The source code does not have to be licensed in a particular way, so long as you share it. The code itself does not need to be on GitHub, either.
The "novel" is defined however you want. It could be 50,000 repetitions of the word "meow". It could literally grab a random novel from Project Gutenberg.
Please try to respect copyright. We're not going to police it, as ultimately it's on your head if you want to just copy/paste a Stephen King novel or whatever

atoms.span: NaNoGenMo (National Novel Generation Month) is an annual programming challenge
managed by maintainers like Darius Kazemi and Hugo van Kemenade
Write and run code between November 1 (12:01 am GMT) and December 1 (12:01 am GMT) to output a text work of 50,000+ words.
Participants share both the generated text and the source code at the end of the event.
Created as a playful programming spoof of NaNoWriMo (National Novel Writing Month)

observations.notes: The event composed at its grain from its own page, its period and its sharing rule exact. The Project Gutenberg example that marks a generated novel as made from existing text is replaced by a list of techniques, and the page's unpoliced copyright request is given as a rule.
